subtype: Approach: asking the manager for explicit expectations [Action]
passage: With appraisal season six weeks away and his manager Urmila about to leave on a work trip, Chaitanya caught her at the pantry. "Can I take ten minutes tomorrow? I want to ask what a promotion would need, and by when." She looked surprised, then nodded. The next morning she named three gaps: presenting to senior people, mentoring a junior, and owning a project from start to finish. "By the September review." He wrote them down and read them back to check. "Could we look at progress once a month?" Urmila put a recurring slot on both calendars before she left for the airport, and Chaitanya walked back to his desk feeling both nervous and steadier.

qa.q: What three gaps did Urmila name?
qa.a: Urmila named presenting to senior people, mentoring a junior, and owning a project from start to finish.

qa.q: How did Chaitanya feel after the conversation?
qa.a: Chaitanya felt both nervous and steadier.

qa.q: What else could Chaitanya do to work on the gaps, and why?
qa.a: Chaitanya could pick one small chance this month to present to seniors, because early practice shows progress at the monthly reviews.

qa.q: How might Urmila have felt when asked so directly?
qa.a: Urmila was probably surprised at first and then pleased, since Chaitanya's clear question made it easy to set expectations.

grounding: Illustrates asking the manager directly what a promotion requires and by when, getting three named gaps and agreeing on monthly reviews.
